terms.grammar: noun, third declension, masculine or feminine
terms.comment: A member of a state with its rights, against a foreigner (peregrīnus) or an enemy (hostis), of either sex (Lewis & Short). Citizenship is cīvitās (Traupman 178); my fellow citizens, cīvēs meī (Traupman 291); a citizen who holds no office, prīvātus (see individual).

phrases.latin: Rōmānus sum … cīvis; C. Mūcium vocant.
phrases.english: I am a Roman citizen; my name is Gaius Mucius.

sources: Lewis & Short: civis · Lewis & Short: civitas
